ORDER RE: DEFENDANT'S MOTION TO STRIKE (GRANTED IN PART, DENIED IN PART)

LAW AND MOTION 302, DEFENDANT HERMAN FRANK'S MOTION TO STRIKE 1ST AMENDED COMPLAINT. NO APPEARANCE ON THIS MATTER. RULING: THE COURT ADOPTED ITS TENTATIVE RULING - GRANTED AS TO THE SECOND CAUSE OF ACTION FOR NEGLIGENCE, AND DENIED AS TO THE FIRST CAUSE OF ACTION FOR MALICIOUS PROSECUTION. IT IS UNDISPUTED THAT THIS ACTION DERIVES FROM PRIOR LITIGATION, AND THUS DEFENDANT FRANCK HAS MET HIS INITIAL BURDEN OF PROOF. "LITIGATION IS ACTIVITY PROTECTED BY THE SPEECH AND PETITION CLAUSES." (DRUMMOND V. DESMARAIS (2009) 176 CAL.APP.4TH 439, 449.) FOR THE FIRST CAUSE OF ACTION, PLAINTIFFS HAVE MET THEIR SHIFTING BURDEN SHOWING A LIKELIHOOD OF PREVAILING ON THE MERITS FOR MALICIOUS PROSECUTION. (SEE CONTEMPORARY SERVICES CORP. V. STAFF PRO INC. (2007) 152 CAL.APP.4TH 1043, 1056.) PLAINTIFFS OBTAINED A FAVORABLE DETERMINATION OF THE MERITS IN NARRON V. GRAY (CASE NO. CUD-12-641735). THE ENTRY OF JUDGMENT WAS BASED ON THE SUBSTANTIVE MERITS; DEFENDANT NARRON WAS NOT A PROPER PLAINTIFF TO SEEK THE EVICTION OF PLAINTIFFS. DEFENDANTS LACKED PROBABLE CAUSE IN FILING THE UNDERLYING ACTION. PLAINTIFFS HAVE DEMONSTRATED MALICE BY DEFENDANTS IN THEIR CONTINUED PROSECUTION OF THE UNDERLYING ACTION DESPITE KNOWING THAT DEFENDANT NARRON WAS NOT A PROPER PLAINTIFF. FOR THE SECOND CAUSE OF ACTION, THE NEGLIGENCE CLAIM IS BARRED BY THE LITIGATION PRIVILEGE. (CIV. CODE 47(B).) "THE ONLY EXCEPTION TO APPLICATION OF SECTION 47[(B)] TO TORT SUITS HAS BEEN FOR MALICIOUS PROSECUTION ACTIONS." (SILBERG V. ANDERSON (1990) 50 CAL.3D 205, 215.) ORDER SIGNED IN OPEN COURT. JUDGE: ERNEST H. GOLDSMITH, CLERK: LESLEY FISCELLA, REPORTER: DEBORAH NEVILLE 	703.

ORDER RE: DEFENDANT NARRON'S SPECIAL MOTION TO STRIKE FIRST AMENDED COMPLAINT FOR DAMAGES (SLAPP)

LAW AND MOTION, 302, DEFENDANT MARGARET NARRON'S SPECIAL MOTION TO STRIKE 1ST AMENDED COMPLAINT IS DENIED. THE MOTION IS DENIED AS MOOT AS TO THE NEGLIGENCE CAUSE OF ACTION BECAUSE PLAINTIFF DISMISSED THAT CLAIM LONG BEFORE DEFENDANT FILED THIS MOTION. THE MOTION IS DENIED AS TO THE MALICIOUS PROSECUTION CAUSE OF ACTION. DEFENDANT HAS MET THE FIRST PRONG OF CCP 425.16 AND SHOWN THAT THE MALICIOUS PROSECUTION CLAIM ARISES FROM PETITIONING ACTIVITY. PLAINTIFFS HAVE MET THE SECOND PRONG AND SHOWN A PROBABILITY OF PREVAILING ON THE MERITS. "THE DETERMINATION OF THE REASONS UNDERLYING THE DISMISSAL IS A QUESTION OF FACT." HAIGHT V. HANDWEILER (1988) 199 CAL.APP.3D 85. HERE, IT IS NOT CLEAR THAT THE DISMISSAL WAS BASED ON A LACK OF STANDING. AS THE COURT OF APPEAL FOUND, IT COULD EQUALLY BE BASED ON A FAILURE TO PROSECUTE, WHICH IS A TERMINATION ON THE MERITS. SEE MINASIAN V. SAPSE (1978) 80 CAL.APP.3D 823, 827. ORDER SIGNED IN OPEN COURT. JUDGE: A. JAMES ROBERTSON II; CLERK: CYNTHIA HERBERT; REPORTER : MELANIE GHENO, CSR # 7489 =302/AJR
